newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK police search for children feared thrown overboard.
newsitem.headline: HK police search for children feared thrown overboard.

text.p: Hong Kong police are searching nearby waters for several mainland Chinese children thought to have been thrown from a vessel trying to sneak into the territory, a spokeswoman said on Saturday.
The search was launched after a police patrol vessel chase an unlit speedboat late on Friday. Police saw two objects being thrown into the sea, the police spokeswoman told Reuters.
Another officer told a Hong Kong radio station he believed the objects were children. He said his colleagues had seen two men and four or five children on the speedboat during the chase.
The rescue mission, around the Ninepin islands southeast of Hong Kong island, involved five police launches and one helicopter but nothing had been found, the spokeswoman said.
"At around 11 pm (1500 GMT) last night, a police patrol craft spotted a speedboat and gave chase," she said.
"Police saw some objects being pushed into the sea but we cannot confirm if they are children," she said.
The search was still on, she said.

A growing number of illegal Chinese immigrants, including children, have been caught along border areas in recent weeks after rumours began spreading in southern China that amnesty would be given to illegal migrant children.
But the Hong Kong government has repeatedly stressed that everybody, including children, would be sent back.
An influx of illegal immigrants from China is a major concern in the territory, which reverts to Chinese rule at midnight on June 30 after more than 150 years of British colonial rule.
